summary: A blank line separates top-level declarations: after the imports, and around every function, class, interface, enum and multi-line statement. One-line constants and type aliases may sit together.
why: Whitespace is paragraphs. A file reads like a chapter when each declaration stands on its own, and a wall of code with no blank lines hides where one thing ends and the next begins.
note: Imports and re-exports such as `export { a } from './a'` stay grouped, and so do constants, even when one of them spans several lines. `oxlint --fix` adds the missing blank lines.
